text:
Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

Before I write it, a few questions. Your answers will change what the page says:

1. **What do you do for salons that a general bookkeeper doesn't?** For example: tips, commission or tiered pay, booth renters vs. employees, taxable retail sales vs. non-taxable services, or the reports from your clients' booking systems. This will probably be the core of the page, so concrete examples help most.
2. **Who's the main reader?** Is it an owner doing their own books at midnight, one leaving another bookkeeper, or one whose accountant keeps sending everything back? I'll write the opening for that person.
3. **Should the page mention the price increase and the three missed closes?** I'd suggest one short line on each, said plainly. For example: "the 10th, every month (I missed it three times last year, and told those clients ahead of time)." If that's true, the honesty builds trust. Is it fine to include them, and what actually happened when you missed?
4. **What name and location should I use?** Give me your name or business name, plus the state or area you serve. Sales tax rules depend on the state, so naming yours tells the reader you know their rules.
5. **What happens on the 20-minute call, and when can people book it?** For example: do you look at their current books, and do you give them a yes/no on fit? Also, what should the button say, if you have a preference?

If you don't know or don't want to share something, just say so and I'll leave it out instead of guessing.

1. I managed a hair salon for 6 years before I became a bookkeeper. I can't get more specific than that right now.

2. I don't know. I haven't thought about it that way.

3. Yes, include both, one short line each.
   - **Price:** I raised it because I added payroll for up to 10 staff, which I didn't do before.
   - **Missed closes:** I'm not sure I told those clients ahead of time, so don't say that. Since January, if I miss the 10th, that month's fee is free.

4. Carla Benson, business is Chair and Ledger. I don't have a location to give you.

5. I don't have more detail on what happens in the call. The button goes to my calendar, and calls are Tuesday to Saturday. No preference on the button wording.

Here's the page, about 340 words.

<final_document>
# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons. Only salons.

I'm Carla Benson. Before I became a bookkeeper, I managed a hair salon for six years. Now I run Chair and Ledger, and I work only with hair and nail salons.

You run the salon. I'll keep the books, run payroll and file your sales tax, every month.

## What you get

- **Monthly books**, closed by the 10th of the following month.
- **Payroll** for up to 10 staff.
- **Sales tax filing.**

All three are included for $199 a month.

## How it's gone so far

I work with 31 salons right now. Two left last year, and both left because they sold their salons.

Last tax season, nine of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because their books came in clean. One said she saved $800. I can't promise you the same, because that depends on your accountant. Clean books are the part I can promise.

## The things you should know up front

**The 10th.** I missed it three times last year. Since January, if I miss the 10th, you don't pay for that month.

**The price.** It's $199 a month. Until January it was $149. I raised it for everyone, including my existing clients, because I added payroll for up to 10 staff, which I didn't offer before.

**It's just me.** I'm one person, so the person who answers your questions is the person doing your books. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.

## Start with a free 20-minute call

The first call is free and takes 20 minutes. Pick a time that works for you, any day from Tuesday to Saturday.

**[Book your free 20-minute call]**
</final_document>

A few notes:

- **The 10th:** the "fee is free" promise started in January, and last year's three misses happened before it. Check that this is right, because a reader could fairly ask whether you've missed since.
- **Salon experience:** the page says almost nothing specific about salon work beyond your six years as a manager. That's the weakest part. When you have time, one or two concrete examples would make it much stronger, like how you handle tips, commission pay or booth renters.
- **The $800 client:** I kept "she" because that's how you described them.
